summary: Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under Shinobu Yamaguchi and Shogo Watanabe, later serving there as a visiting researcher and working at the Cabinet Office in 2020.
Sayori Tsubota is an Indology researcher who pursued doctoral studies at Osaka University (attested 2020) and held a JSPS postdoctoral fellow (PD) appointment at Tohoku University (attested 2026).
Scarlett J. He works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She has held a post at Columbia University, where she is also attested as a PhD student in 2026.

Schuyler Cammann (1912–1991) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Yale, Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and under doctoral supervisor Helmut Hoffmann, he was a long-time faculty member at the University of Pennsylvania (~1948–1982).

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne and has held appointments at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.
Scott DeLancey (born 1949) is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied under Yungdrung Manang and held a post at the University of Oregon around 1982.

Scott Hurley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison, earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, and became an associate professor at Luther College in 2002.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, he held posts at Hebrew University, ANU, and the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, also studying there under several teachers, and held an academic post at SOAS (attested 1996).

Sebastian Nehrdich works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Hamburg, Kyoto, and Düsseldorf (PhD 2023), he has held posts at the University of Hamburg, University of Düsseldorf, Tohoku University, and UC Berkeley.
Sebastian Pole is a specialist in Indology and other fields who pursued studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado (1855–1922) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Pontifical Institute of Saint Apollinaris (~1887–1889) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Curso Superior de Letras (1907) and the University of Lisbon (1917).
See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi (born 1961) is a historian who earned her doctorate from the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She has taught at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia (~2008–2020), and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893), where he later served as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905), and founded Bussho Kankōkai.

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, obtaining a doctorate, and served on Kyoto University's faculty and at its Institute for Research in Humanities.

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) and held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1965–1993), Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and other fields. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, he became a professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and later at Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Komazawa University (attested 1986), he held appointments there (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2005–2008) and became a professor there around 2012.
